question.text: For a trust, applying Rule 9 of the PMLA Rules as reproduced in the IFSCA AML/CFT workbook, which of the following must be identified as beneficial owners?

answer.text: The author of the trust, the trustee, beneficiaries with 10% or more interest, and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control
Only the trustee and the named beneficiaries
Only the author (settlor) of the trust
Only beneficiaries with more than 50% interest in the trust

explanation.text: The Logic: Rule 9 of the PMLA (Maintenance of Records) Rules, as set out on p.46 and p.101 of the IFSCA AML/CFT workbook, requires identification of (i) the author of the trust; (ii) the trustee; (iii) beneficiaries with 10% or more interest in the trust; and (iv) any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control through a chain of control or ownership. All four categories together form option A. The Trap: Option B drops the author/settlor and the controllers. Option C drops everyone except the settlor. Option D uses a 50% threshold which does not match Rule 9. The original audit flagged that p.100 of the same workbook (in the IFSCA Guidelines section) used a 15% threshold for trust beneficiaries, creating an internal workbook conflict. Note: The original question was ambiguous because of the workbook's internal conflict between the Rule 9 / p.101 ten-percent threshold and the p.100 IFSCA Guidelines fifteen-percent threshold. The stem has been tightened to anchor the answer to Rule 9 as reproduced in the workbook, so that the 10% formulation is unambiguously correct. Source: NISM-IFSCA-01 AML/CFT in the IFSC (Dec 2025), pp.46, 101.
